land.text: the Kadamba kingdom of Banavasi, which Pulakeshin I took over (Chalukya page footnote: 'overpowered his overlord in c. 540 and took control of the Kadamba kingdom'); Cliopatria's Chalukya shape of 555 is used for it

predecessors.note: The kadamba-empire dossier ends in 540 (the page's c. 540 footnote); the infobox of the Chalukya page gives 'Established: 543'.

land.text: the Chalukya remnant of the south that Dantidurga's Rashtrakuta successors took; Kirtivarman II 'retained control over his southern provinces up to the year 757'

successors.note: Dantidurga defeated the Chalukyas in 753 (Ellora record) and took the north; the south fell by 757. Cliopatria's Rashtrakuta row starts 755.

land.text: Vengi, the coast of Andhra from Visakhapatnam to Guntur held after the conquest of the Vishnukundina kingdom (Pulakeshin II page: 'Vishakhapatnam to Nellore and Guntur')

successors.note: Infobox lists the Eastern Chalukyas as a successor; Kubja Vishnuvardhana's Vengi 'claimed independence by 641' (Pulakeshin II page), so the land left long before 757.

capitals.name: Vatapi (Badami)
capitals.note: Pulakeshin I 'took Vatapi (modern Badami) under his control and made it his capital'. Occupied by the Pallavas 642-655; the page does not say where the Chalukya court sat in that time. The Rashtrakutas' Manyakheta is named for Dantidurga but the Chalukya seat stays Badami to the end.

correction.text: the Cliopatria shape of 555 (Karnataka around Vatapi, c. 203,000 km2) stretched back to 543; the page says only that Pulakeshin I 'took control of the Kadamba kingdom'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria starts the Chalukyas in 555 but the infobox gives 'Established: 543'. The page gives no area (infobox silent) and no conquests of Pulakeshin I, Kirtivarman I or Mangalesha, so the 555 core is stretched back; the ledger's 543 event carries the birth.

203,000 km2 for 555-601: the Kadamba heartland in Karnataka. The Chalukya page gives no area; its 'Kaveri in the south to the Narmada in the north' is the peak, not this period. Mangalesha's inscriptions (578, 595) and Kirtivarman I's conquests are undated or absent on the page, so the shape stands.

correction.text: the Cliopatria shape of 602 unchanged, valid 602-615 only

keyframe_review.note: Shape unchanged but its years end in 615 (Cliopatria 602-622): the Chalukya page has 'Conquered the eastern Deccan in 616', which the next new keyframe adds. The 602 step (+17,000 km2, the Rayalaseema border of the Pallavas) is not on the pages opened; the Pulakeshin II page says only that the Banas 'appear to have been Pallava feudatories before submitting to Pulakeshin'. [orchestrator 2 Nov 2026: from/to set to 602..615 from this entry's own 'valid 602-615 only'; without them the compiler drew the shape for all its Cliopatria years, overlapping the next keyframe (window p1100-p1199 report)]

union.text: Vengi, the coast of Andhra from Visakhapatnam to Guntur held after the conquest of the Vishnukundina kingdom (Pulakeshin II page: 'Vishakhapatnam to Nellore and Guntur')

correction.text: the Karnataka core of 602 plus the Vengi coast of Andhra taken from the Vishnukundinas, from 616 (Cliopatria has the east only from 626)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 616-622: the Chalukya page says the dynasty 'Conquered the eastern Deccan in 616' and 'appointed his brother Kubja Vishnuvardhana as Viceroy in 621'; Cliopatria adds the eastern lands only in 626. The shape is the 602 core with the Vengi coast.

union.text: Vengi, the coast of Andhra from Visakhapatnam to Guntur held after the conquest of the Vishnukundina kingdom (Pulakeshin II page: 'Vishakhapatnam to Nellore and Guntur')

correction.text: the 623 shape plus the Vengi coast held since 616

keyframe_review.note: 525,000 km2 for 623-625: the Maharashtra block ('three Maharashtrakas', 99,000 villages) and Telangana's edge are in, but the Vengi coast taken in 616 is missing until 626. The page gives no area figure; the conquests of the Latas, Malavas and Gurjaras are undated (Aihole inscription, 634).

750,000 km2 for 626-632: Telangana, southern Chhattisgarh and southern Odisha are inside (the 626 shape holds 45,000 km2 of Odisha and 50,000 of Chhattisgarh). Kalinga and Kosala 'accepted Pulakeshin's suzerainty without offering any resistance', so they are drawn direct by Cliopatria but belong in the vassal tint (ledger). Extent agrees with the page: 'Vishakhapatnam to Nellore and Guntur under his control'.

928,000 km2, the peak: adds the Narmada frontier (Madhya Pradesh 77,000 km2, southern Gujarat 12,000 km2) of the Malavas, Latas and Gurjaras, all listed in the Aihole inscription of 634. The page has the empire 'from the Narmada River in the north to the Krishna-Godavari region in the east', and the Chalukya page 'from the Kaveri in the south to the Narmada in the north': consistent. No infobox area to compare.

minus.text: Vengi, the coast of Andhra from Visakhapatnam to Guntur held after the conquest of the Vishnukundina kingdom (Pulakeshin II page: 'Vishakhapatnam to Nellore and Guntur')

correction.text: the 644 shape without Vengi, which broke away by 641 as the Eastern Chalukyas; Vatapi's district is Pallava-occupied (ledger)

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria keeps the peak shape (928,000 km2) for 644-655, but Vengi 'claimed independence by 641' and the Pallavas held Vatapi from 642: the Chalukya history of those years is 'unclear' (Vikramaditya I page). Vengi is removed here; the occupied capital is a ledger occupation. The rest stays at low confidence.

minus.text: Vengi, the coast of Andhra from Visakhapatnam to Guntur held after the conquest of the Vishnukundina kingdom (Pulakeshin II page: 'Vishakhapatnam to Nellore and Guntur')

correction.text: the 647 shape without Vengi (independent as the Eastern Chalukyas by 641)

keyframe_review.note: Same correction for 647-655: the peak shape without Vengi; Vikramaditya I 'declared himself king of the Chalukyas (655)' and ended a Pallava occupation that 'had lasted for thirteen years'.

805,000 km2 for 656-660: Vikramaditya I 'recovered most of its territories it controlled under Pulakeshin II'; the 656 shape drops the Vengi coast and most of Odisha, which fits Vengi's independence and the end of the Kalinga suzerainty (the page gives no borders).

804,000 km2 for 661-731: the recovered Chalukya kingdom through Vikramaditya I (655-680), Vijayaditya (696-733). The Pallava raids (Kanchipuram c. 670; Peruvalanallur 674) moved no border on the page. No infobox area to compare.

810,000 km2 for 732-749: +5,000 km2 in southern Gujarat, the Lata branch under Pulakeshin Avanijanashraya, who 'fought and defeated an Umayyad army in 739' (page). The step in 732 itself is undated on the page.

minus.text: Madhya Pradesh and southern Gujarat, which Dantidurga controlled by 750

correction.text: the 750 shape without Madhya Pradesh and southern Gujarat, which Dantidurga held 'By 750 AD'; valid 750-752

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria keeps the whole empire to 754, but the Dantidurga page says 'By 750 AD' he controlled Madhya Pradesh and southern Gujarat, and the Ellora record has him defeat the Chalukyas in 753. This shape is valid 750-752 without Madhya Pradesh and Gujarat; the 753-757 keyframe is the next one.

correction.text: the Cliopatria shape of 755 unchanged, valid 753-757

keyframe_review.note: 209,000 km2: the southern remnant (Karnataka, Rayalaseema). Shape unchanged but its years are 753-757: the Ellora record 'defeated the Chalukyas in 753' and Kirtivarman II 'retained control over his southern provinces up to the year 757' (Vakkaleri inscription).

region.text: the Kadamba kingdom around Vatapi that Pulakeshin I took

ledger.note: 543: Pulakeshin I founds the Chalukya dynasty at Vatapi. 'The Chalukya dynasty was established by Pulakeshin I in 543'; he 'took Vatapi (modern Badami...) under his control and made it his capital'. A footnote has him overpower 'his overlord in c. 540 and took control of the Kadamba kingdom'. The page gives the cities, not a boundary.

region.text: the land Cliopatria's 602 shape adds to the 555 shape, on the Pallava border (Rayalaseema, per the late-pallava-empire dossier)

ledger.note: 602: a step in the Pallava border. The pages opened do not date it; the Pulakeshin II page notes the Banas 'appear to have been Pallava feudatories before submitting to Pulakeshin'. Date and land are from Cliopatria's 602 shape and the late-pallava-empire dossier.

region.text: Vengi, the coast of Andhra from Visakhapatnam to Guntur held after the conquest of the Vishnukundina kingdom (Pulakeshin II page: 'Vishakhapatnam to Nellore and Guntur')

ledger.note: 616: Pulakeshin II conquers the eastern Deccan. 'Conquered the eastern Deccan in 616'; he 'invaded and captured Pishtapura' and took the Vishnukundina kingdom (Pulakeshin II page), and 'appointed his brother Kubja Vishnuvardhana as Viceroy in 621'. The Vishnukundina rule ends in 624 on their own dossier.

region.text: the 'three Maharashtrakas', said to include 99,000 villages

ledger.note: 623: Maharashtra comes under the Chalukyas. 'He controlled the three Maharashtrakas, said to include 99,000 villages' (Pulakeshin II page, undated); the year is Cliopatria's 623 step and the Kalachuri dossier's c. 625. Pulakeshin II also 'besieged' the Mauryas of Konkana's capital Puri (undated).

union.text: Vengi, the coast of Andhra from Visakhapatnam to Guntur held after the conquest of the Vishnukundina kingdom (Pulakeshin II page: 'Vishakhapatnam to Nellore and Guntur')

region.text: the conquered Vishnukundina kingdom 'in the lower Godavari-Krishna valley'

ledger.note: 626: the Vishnukundina lands are Chalukya. Pulakeshin II 'conquered the Vishnukundina kingdom in the lower Godavari-Krishna valley' after a battle near Kunala Lake (Kolleru); the Vishnukundina dossier ends the dynasty in 624, Cliopatria adds Telangana in 626.

region.text: Kalinga

ledger.note: 626: Kalinga accepts Chalukya suzerainty. 'accepted Pulakeshin's suzerainty without offering any resistance' (Aihole inscription, 634); the year is Cliopatria's step to southern Odisha, the page gives none.

region.text: Kosala, probably the Panduvamshi realm of Dakshina Kosala

ledger.note: 626: Kosala accepts Chalukya suzerainty. Same Aihole sentence as Kalinga; 'Kosala was probably the Panduvamshi realm of Dakshina Kosala'. Year from Cliopatria's 626 shape.

region.text: Malwa and Lata, the Narmada frontier of the Malavas, Latas and Gurjaras

ledger.note: 633: the Narmada frontier. 'The Aihole inscription credits him with subjugating them'; 'Lata was later governed by a Chalukya governor'. The inscription is of 634; the year is Cliopatria's 633 step. Some 'may have submitted without a fight'.

region.text: Vengi, the coast of Andhra from Visakhapatnam to Guntur held after the conquest of the Vishnukundina kingdom (Pulakeshin II page: 'Vishakhapatnam to Nellore and Guntur')

ledger.note: 641: Vengi breaks away. Kubja Vishnuvardhana 'acknowledged his suzerainty in 631 but claimed independence by 641, founding the Eastern Chalukya line of Vengi'. The year is 'by 641'.

region.text: Vatapi (Badami) and its district, occupied by the Pallavas for thirteen years

ledger.note: 642: the Pallavas take Vatapi. 'Pallava Narasimhavarman however reversed this victory in 642 by attacking and occupying Badami temporarily'; Pulakeshin II was 'probably killed' (Pulakeshin II page). Hatched, not an annexation; the page does not say how far the occupation reached.

region.text: Vatapi (Badami) and its district, occupied by the Pallavas for thirteen years

ledger.note: 655: Vikramaditya I retakes Vatapi. 'Vikramaditya then declared himself king of the Chalukyas (655)'; he 'was able to end Pallava's occupation, which had lasted for thirteen years'.

region.text: Kalinga

ledger.note: 656: the Kalinga suzerainty is over. Cliopatria's 656 shape drops most of Odisha; the Vikramaditya I page is silent on Kalinga and gives no borders for the recovered kingdom.

region.text: Kanchipuram, which Vikramaditya I 'seized'

ledger.note: 670: Vikramaditya I seizes Kanchipuram. Paramesvaravarman I was 'attacked by the Chalukyan king Vikramaditya I and seized Kanchipuram after defeating him'; Western Chalukya records give 'A.D. 670' (Honnur plates c. 670-671).

region.text: the Pallava heartland

ledger.note: 674: the Pallavas win at Peruvalanallur. 'In the ensuing Battle of Puruvalanallur in 674 with Vikramaditya's forces, the Pallavas defeated the Chalukyas'; no land changed hands.

region.text: the Lata branch of the Chalukyas in southern Gujarat

ledger.note: 739: the Arabs invade the Lata country. Pulakeshin Avanijanashraya, 'governor of the Lata branch', 'fought and defeated an Umayyad army in 739 CE'; Navsari itself is not on the page.

region.text: the Lata branch

ledger.note: 739: the Umayyad army is beaten, the frontier holds ('fought and defeated an Umayyad army in 739 CE').

region.text: Kanchipuram, entered by Vikramaditya II

ledger.note: c. 742: Vikramaditya II enters Kanchipuram. 'The road to Kanchipuram lay open and Vikramaditya II entered the city victorious'; the page gives no year ('after 734'; earliest mention the Narwan plates of 21 December 741 or 742), so the year is the plates', a bridging date.

region.text: the Pallava heartland

ledger.note: c. 744: the Chalukya raid on Kanchi is over. 'The final invasion of Kanchipuram happened in the final years of the reign of Vikramaditya II' (reign 733-744); Dantidurga 'helped Nandivarman II to recover Kanchi' (undated). No land held.

region.text: Madhya Pradesh and southern Gujarat, which Dantidurga controlled by 750

ledger.note: 750: Dantidurga holds Malwa and south Gujarat. 'By 750 AD' he controlled Madhya Pradesh and southern Gujarat; he 'defeated the kings of Lata (Gujarat), Malwa, Tanka, Kalinga and Sheshas' (undated). Cliopatria keeps them Chalukya to 754.

minus.text: Madhya Pradesh and southern Gujarat, which Dantidurga controlled by 750

region.text: the northern Chalukya empire: Maharashtra, Telangana and the east, lost when Dantidurga 'defeated the Chalukyas in 753'

ledger.note: 753: Dantidurga overthrows the Chalukya empire. The Ellora record 'narrates that he defeated the Chalukyas in 753'; the Chalukya page says Kirtivarman II 'was overthrown by the Rashtrakuta king Dantidurga in 753'. The page does not name the lands; the drawn land is what Cliopatria's 755 shape no longer holds.

region.text: Dakshina Kosala

ledger.note: 753: Kosala goes with the north. The Dantidurga page is silent on Kosala; Chhattisgarh is outside Cliopatria's 755 shape.

region.text: the Chalukya remnant of the south

ledger.note: 757: the last Chalukya province falls. Kirtivarman II 'retained control over his southern provinces up to the year 757' (Vakkaleri inscription); Cliopatria ends the Chalukyas in 756 and the infobox in 753. The page does not say who took the south; Krishna I 'extended the kingdom across Karnataka'.

wars.name: Pulakeshin II's war with Harsha

zones.text: the Narmada, the frontier where Harsha was stopped

wars.outcome: Chalukya victory: Harsha 'advanced up to the Narmada River before being forced to retreat'; the Narmada became the frontier. No land changed hands, so no contest is drawn.
wars.note: Dated 'winter of 618-619' by Bapat and Sohoni, 'around 612 CE or earlier' by Ramesh and Sastri.

wars.name: Chalukya conquest of Vengi

zones.text: Vengi, the coast of Andhra from Visakhapatnam to Guntur held after the conquest of the Vishnukundina kingdom (Pulakeshin II page: 'Vishakhapatnam to Nellore and Guntur')

wars.outcome: Chalukya victory: Pishtapura captured, a battle near Kunala Lake (Kolleru), the Vishnukundina kingdom conquered and Kubja Vishnuvardhana made governor.
wars.note: 'Conquered the eastern Deccan in 616' (Chalukya page); the Vishnukundina dynasty ends in 624.

wars.name: Pallava-Chalukya war under Pulakeshin II

zones.text: Vatapi (Badami) and its district, occupied by the Pallavas for thirteen years

wars.outcome: Pulakeshin II's drive reached Kanchipuram with setbacks at Pariyala, Suramara and Manimangala; Narasimhavarman I then took Vatapi in 642 and held it for thirteen years until Vikramaditya I retook it in 655.
wars.note: The page dates the Pallava capture 'c. 642-643'; the occupation is the ledger's 642-655.

wars.name: Vikramaditya I's wars with the Pallavas
wars.outcome: Vikramaditya I seized Kanchipuram c. 670 but 'the Pallavas defeated the Chalukyas' at Peruvalanallur in 674; no border moved.

wars.name: Vikramaditya II's Pallava campaigns
wars.outcome: Raids on Kanchipuram around 730 and after 734 (Nandivarman II, aged thirteen, failed to stop them); no annexation on the page.
wars.note: Years from 'Around 730', 'after 734' and the Narwan plates of 741/742.

wars.name: Arab invasion of Lata
wars.outcome: The Chalukya governor Pulakeshin Avanijanashraya 'fought and defeated an Umayyad army in 739 CE'.

wars.name: Rashtrakuta overthrow of the Chalukyas
wars.outcome: Dantidurga took Madhya Pradesh and Gujarat by 750, defeated the Chalukyas in 753, and Kirtivarman II held the south until 757.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line exists on the pages. The Narmada is the one named frontier (after the Harsha war) but is still a river zone, not a surveyed line; vassal lands (Kalinga, Kosala) have no border at all.

notes: Five pages (the budget). The Chalukya page has no infobox area, so Cliopatria's areas could not be compared; extents are checked against the sentences 'from the Kaveri in the south to the Narmada in the north' and 'Vishakhapatnam to Nellore and Guntur'. Dates: the infobox says Established 543 and Disestablished 753; a footnote has Pulakeshin I take the Kadamba kingdom c. 540 (the kadamba-empire dossier ends 540); Cliopatria runs 555-756. This dossier uses 543-757 (Vakkaleri inscription: the south held to 757). Kalinga and Dakshina Kosala are vassals from the Aihole inscription (634) but the pages give no end; the Kalinga tint ends 656 where Cliopatria drops Odisha, Kosala's at 753 (confidence 1). Chhattisgarh stays inside Cliopatria's shape to 754. The 642-655 interregnum is 'unclear' on the pages: only the Vengi loss and the Pallava occupation of Vatapi are applied. The 602, 623, 732 steps are undated on the pages. Counterparts that need dossiers: eastern-chalukyas (sa-03-x), Kalachuris of Mahishmati (exists), 'Mauryas of Konkana', 'Malavas, Latas and Gurjaras' (names only). The occupation events follow the Tang example (the owner's dossier names the occupier as counterpart). Gazetteer: Badami, Vatapi and Aihole are not places (a coordinate radius is used).
